references.text: God gives Moses commands and statutes that he is to teach the people, in the same way as in Deuteronomy 5:31.
The Lord calls Moses up on the mountain to receive the commands and the law that he is to teach the people.
Moses urges the people to listen to the statutes and laws that he teaches them, so that they may live and enter the land.
Moses explains that he has taught them statutes and laws as the Lord commanded him, so that they may follow them in the land they are about to take possession of.
The Lord commands Moses to teach the people commands, statutes, and laws that they are to keep in the land they are about to take possession of.
The people shall keep all the statutes and laws when they enter the land the Lord gives them.
The statutes and laws that the people are to keep in the land the Lord gives them as their possession.
Joshua is commanded to keep the entire law that Moses gave, as a continuation of what Moses received from the Lord.
Moses was faithful as a servant in God's house to testify to what would be spoken, referring to his role as mediator of God's commands.
